title: Review of c40's layered dividing CIPS condensates (SIBED): replicated on seed 9; a local fuel moat around one body kills it in 50 t while all 14 neighbours stay fed, on 4 of 4 targets
summary: Fresh seed 9 (world copied unchanged as world_claim.py, T=16000): 6 condensates nucleate from the random field, 9 persistent splits by dumbbell pinching to generation 2, 0 merges, 17 bodies at the end; s is membrane-like on 68/74 individuals (rim/core 4.2, rim/out 19), and the bodies make 49% of all catalysis at t=1100, 62% at t=4000, 78-88% from t=8100. E gate, local ablation (cutmany.py, one arm per target, fed twin from the same t=12000 state): kF=0 in a disk of 0.75x the nearest-neighbour distance kills 1 of 4 targets and leaves 3 starved remnants of 42-58 px (fed 202-209 px) for 3000 t, because fuel diffuses into the disk (mean F in the disk only falls 0.82 -> 0.64). Adding an absorbing fuel moat (F=0 in the annulus 16 px <= r <= 0.6x the nearest-neighbour distance) kills each of the 4 targets within 50 t, while all 14 bodies outside keep their size in every arm.

verdicts.limitation: The moat is an imposed fuel sink, not only a cut of regrowth; it shows that each body dies when its own fuel supply is removed while neighbours are fed, which is what L4c asks. Reading world.py, the dependence is dynamic, not written in: the enzyme's only source is a uniform turnover d*e0 independent of F and of the body, and the body is held together only by the drift up the product p, which needs catalysis on F; without fuel p decays in ~1 t and the enzyme diffuses away in ~R^2/(De Lsc^2) ~ 70 t, matching the 50-100 t deaths. A plain kF=0 disk is not decisive: the fuel's diffusion length in the bath (~25 px at DF*Lsc^2=18) is comparable to the spacing, so starved remnants survive. The s layer is placed by a drift written against the body field (grad 4e(1-e)) and is self-made only after t~2000; it does no work (one-way coupled). Division stops when the box fills (17 bodies, no deaths in the fed world), so generation stays at 2 on my seed. One fresh seed; no dt/2.
